claims.text: Baseline TiVNbTa is a single-phase BCC dendritic alloy.
Baseline TiVNbTa has a yield strength of about 330 MPa at 1273 K.
Baseline TiVNbTa has about 40% strain capacity at room temperature.
TiVNbTa exhibits limited strength retention at high temperature compared with its room-temperature performance.
The proposed intervention is to add approximately 5–10 at.% W to TiVNbTa.
Added W will be incorporated into the BCC matrix as a solid solution.
W solute atoms will obstruct dislocation motion in TiVNbTa.
W addition will help stabilize the TiVNbTa microstructure at high temperature.
W addition will produce solid-solution strengthening and increased dislocation pinning.
W addition will improve thermal stability by retarding grain-boundary mobility.
The proposed strengthening and stabilization mechanisms will counteract high-temperature yield-strength degradation.
The proposed mechanisms will not significantly compromise ductility.
At 1273 K, W-modified TiVNbTa will have a yield strength approximately 20–30% above the 330 MPa baseline.
At 1273 K, W-modified TiVNbTa will retain at least 30% strain capacity.
W-modified TiVNbTa will perform better as an intermediate heat-transfer layer.
The beneficial effects of W addition are expected over approximately 1000–1300 K.
Excessive W concentration could cause phase instability.
Excessive W concentration could cause a detrimental loss of ductility.

contradictions.description: The prediction permits strain capacity as low as 30%, but the falsification rule rejects a ductility decrease greater than 15% relative to the only quantified baseline of 40%, which would imply a floor of 34%. Moreover, the 40% baseline is specified at room temperature whereas the prediction is at 1273 K, leaving the comparison basis inconsistent.
